title: GitHub Foundations (GH-900)
default_goal: Pass GH-900 and independently use foundational GitHub workflows

sources.title: Study guide for Exam GH-900: GitHub Foundations

objectives.outcome: Describe the purpose and benefits of version control
Explain the difference between Git and GitHub
Identify repositories, commits, and branches and explain their relationships
Describe GitHub accounts, organizations, and enterprise options
Explain and apply GitHub Flow
Use Markdown for clear communication in issues and pull requests
Recognize appropriate uses for GitHub Desktop and GitHub Mobile
Describe README, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, CODEOWNERS, and SECURITY files
Create, organize, and maintain repositories with templates and branches
Add and manage files in a repository
Describe repository insights, stars, feature previews, metrics dashboards, and dependency insights
Recognize repository maintenance and collaboration best practices
Use issues, pull requests, and discussions for the right collaboration purpose
Link pull requests to issues and manage templates, filters, and assignments
Configure notifications for workflow management
Choose and use Gists, Wikis, and GitHub Pages for documentation and sharing
Describe the purpose and capabilities of GitHub Actions
Identify GitHub Copilot code suggestions, agents, Agent Mode, and multi-model capabilities
Distinguish GitHub Copilot Individual, Business, and Enterprise offerings
Describe Codespaces setup, customization, and dev containers
Distinguish github.dev from Codespaces and choose between them
Describe GitHub Projects and layout options
Configure projects, labels, milestones, and workflows
Use saved replies and assignees to streamline communication
Use project insights to track progress and productivity
Secure accounts with two-factor authentication and passkeys
Identify repository and organization access permissions and roles
Explain Enterprise Managed Users and organization-wide Copilot policy management
Describe visibility settings and branch protection rules
Recognize organization settings, teams, and roles
Describe open-source benefits and GitHub Sponsors
Explain how GitHub supports and advances open-source projects
Follow users and organizations to track activity
Describe GitHub Marketplace and its purpose
Explain InnerSource within organizations
Choose forks, templates, and discoverable repositories appropriately
